prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that enabled GLP-1-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I keep a single prize part, B035, for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 files show that the shared concern is the reliability of attribution and not the quality or maturity of the discovery. The discovery chain (incretin physiology, proglucagon processing, the truncated active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, glucose-dependent insulinotropic and satiety actions, receptor biology) has been confirmed independently for decades, and it has produced replicated randomized evidence on glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The three credited names map onto three separable steps: Holst on physiology, Mojsov on identification of the active form, and Drucker on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor action. A citation written around the discovery chain keeps the credit with the people whose findings opened the field. No other shortlisted part combines a physiological discovery with a disease-level outcome of this size and with a clean separation of steps among three people.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakest point and it has not been resolved by the discussion. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested relative to Habener and colleagues, who are outside the credited list, and none of us can settle it from the supplied record. Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide work is the step that turned the biology into a usable drug, and a discovery-framed prize can be read as omitting it. Including her would force out a physiologist. There is also a risk that the prize is read as rewarding a commercially prominent drug class, and long-term safety and durability of obesity treatment are still accruing, although these do not affect the core discovery.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that Knudsen's work is development built on the discovery, so the citation should be explicitly about the hormone and its active form, and that if colleagues find the therapeutic step inseparable we should say so openly. He also wants the historical record on Mojsov verified before the final ballot.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and with the call for transparency. A citation about the hormone and its active form is the honest basis for excluding Knudsen, and it should not be presented as a cost-free choice. I accept his request that the Mojsov record be checked. My own position is that the evidence supports her as a distinct step, and I have not moved to Knudsen. My round-1 willingness to accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov is now conditional on that check producing evidence that her priority is materially weaker than I judge it to be. Without such evidence I do not think the contest over priority is enough to displace her, and I would not displace Holst or Drucker in any case.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius holds the exclusion of Knudsen with less confidence than Perlmann, wants the therapeutic consequence acknowledged, and says B029 is the stronger alternative but is held back from sitting beside B035 by the missing Eshhar attribution.
responses.response: I share her wish to acknowledge the therapeutic consequence, and I think the citation does this by ending on the therapies that GLP-1 biology enabled, without crediting the drug developers as laureates. I agree with her on Eshhar: it is the main reason B029 stays an alternative to B035 and does not become a second part. I also agree with her view that cGAS-STING is early. She tested my round-1 reasoning and I have not changed it. I would only add that if the committee did go to two parts, B029 would have to be limited to June and Sadelain, and that does not solve the Eshhar gap, so it does not move me to a two-part configuration.

responses.point: The chair would resist dropping Holst if Knudsen were included, and asks whose place Knudsen should take if the framing moved to the therapeutic step.
responses.response: On the chair's question, I agree that Holst should not be the name that goes. His incretin physiology is the earliest and most independently replicated part of the chain, and removing it would leave a prize about a peptide with no physiology. If the committee decided the therapeutic step was indispensable, the only defensible trade would be Knudsen for Mojsov, and only if the record check showed Mojsov's priority to be weak. I do not believe that is the case on the present record, so I keep Mojsov. I also keep my earlier position that this would be a decision for the committee as a whole, not for my vote alone.

responses.point: El-Manira keeps optogenetics (B046) as an alternative, on the grounds that it is original and mature, and he also raises the attribution problem for Mojsov.
responses.response: I take the point that optogenetics is mature and original, and the central satiety actions of GLP-1 he describes support the physiological reading of B035 that I prefer. My view on B046 has not changed. It has not changed because the benefit so far is to the experimental toolkit and the credit of six people cannot be divided among three without leaving out Boyden, Bamberg or Miesenböck. That is why I did not include it among my two alternatives. If the committee wanted a second part I would still prefer B029 or B012, for which there is evidence of patient benefit.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B046 second, wants glucose-dependent therapies in the B035 citation and says the physiology-versus-drug-development framing is a matter of judgement, and he would consider B002 only in a later year.
responses.response: I agree that the framing is a matter of judgement, and that is the reason I have settled on a discovery-centred citation. I would not add glucose-dependent therapies as a claim in its own right, because it moves the weight toward the drug, but the phrase on enabled therapies covers the clinical consequence. I agree that B002 can wait, since its attribution is clean but the conceptual change took place long ago. We have co-authored work, as I disclose below, and it has no connection to this position.

uncertainties: Whether the documentary record on the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is enough to support Mojsov relative to Habener-group contributions. I have not seen it verified and I would want the secretariat to check it before the final ballot.
Whether the committee will frame B035 around discovery or around drug development. This determines whether Knudsen displaces anyone.
Whether B012 adds anything to a case that has a long history of earlier recognition, and how to handle the Rowley, Nowell and Witte groundwork if it were chosen.
Long-term safety and outcome data for GLP-1 receptor agonists are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted ballot, including B035, B029 and B012. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén on single-cell work, and I have previously co-authored with Christopher Burge's group. None of these involves a credited name on the shortlist. Shared affiliation with Karolinska Institutet gives no documented tie to any credited person. This is unchanged from round 1.
